components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.hanzi: 快递员上门送包裹。
example.pinyin: Kuàidìyuán shàngmén sòng bāoguǒ.
example.english: The delivery worker came to the door to deliver the package.
example.fact: Amazon's first drone delivery, Prime Air, dropped a package at a customer's door in Cambridge, England in December 2016, just 13 minutes after the order was placed. Modern last-mile delivery networks now route hundreds of millions of packages a day, and doorstep delivery has become the default retail experience in many countries.

components.note: 入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 医生对病人进行了全面检查。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng duì bìngrén jìnxíng le quánmiàn jiǎnchá.
example.english: The doctor gave the patient a comprehensive examination.
example.fact: The annual physical exam traces back to 19th-century life insurance companies, which required medical checkups to assess risk before issuing policies. Today, comprehensive full-body MRI screening is being studied as a way to catch early-stage cancers, though its cost-effectiveness for healthy populations is still debated among physicians.

components.note: 又 (hand, here standing in for 奚, part of the original character) — a simplified stroke that no longer pictures anything on its own.
鸟 (bird) — combined with the simplified left side, 鸡 names a specific 'kind of bird,' the chicken.
尸 (a body) — the body of an animal.
毛 (fur/hair) — trailing behind it, together giving 尾 its meaning 'tail.'
酉 (a wine jar) — the vessel holding the drink
氵 (liquid) — the wine itself inside the jar

example.hanzi: 他在酒吧点了一杯鸡尾酒。
example.pinyin: Tā zài jiǔbā diǎn le yì bēi jīwěijiǔ.
example.english: He ordered a cocktail at the bar.
example.fact: The Manhattan cocktail is said to have been invented in the 1870s at the Manhattan Club in New York City, possibly for a banquet hosted by Winston Churchill's mother, Jennie Jerome. The word 'cocktail' itself first appeared in print in a 1798 British newspaper, though its exact origin is still disputed by etymologists.

meanings: button (one that can be pressed to trigger an action)

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 按 relates to pressing something with the hand
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 按's reading àn, differing only in tone
钅 (metal) — 钮 names a small metal fastener, a button.
丑 (chǒu) gives a sound distantly related to niǔ, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 请按下红色按钮启动机器。
example.pinyin: Qǐng ànxià hóngsè ànniǔ qǐdòng jīqì.
example.english: Please press the red button to start the machine.
example.fact: The international safety standard IEC 60947-5-5 requires emergency-stop buttons to be red, mushroom-shaped, and mounted on a yellow background so operators can find them instantly under stress. The design has barely changed since factory automation became widespread in the mid-20th century.

components.note: 走 (to walk/run) — 超 relates to overtaking or surpassing someone while moving
召 (zhào) gives a sound distantly related to 超's reading chāo, having drifted apart over time
亠 depicts a flag or marker raised above a trading spot.
巾 (cloth) — goods laid out for sale beneath the flag, together giving 市 its meaning 'market, city.'

example.hanzi: 妈妈每周去超市买菜。
example.pinyin: Māma měi zhōu qù chāoshì mǎi cài.
example.english: Mom goes to the supermarket every week to buy groceries.
example.fact: The world's first self-service supermarket, Piggly Wiggly, opened in Memphis, Tennessee in 1916, letting customers pick items off the shelves themselves instead of having a clerk fetch them. The change cut labor costs dramatically and became the template for grocery stores worldwide.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 探 describes reaching out with the hand to search for something.
糸 (thread) — thick strands twisted into a rope
冖 (a covering) — the ceiling or beam the rope hangs from
耂 is a variant of 老 (aged, experienced) forming the top of the character.
白 (white, clear) sits below — the ancient combination is debated, but together it came to mark 'the one who' or 'a person who does something,' as in 探索者 'explorer.'

example.hanzi: 他是一位勇敢的探索者。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi yǒnggǎn de tànsuǒzhě.
example.english: He is a brave explorer.
example.fact: Explorer 1, launched by the United States in January 1958, was the first American satellite to reach orbit, and it discovered the Van Allen radiation belts — bands of charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field. Physicist James Van Allen made the discovery using a simple Geiger counter aboard the satellite, one of the first major scientific results of the Space Age.

components.note: 冂 (a covering or frame, here representing a cart) — 两 pictures two things sharing one enclosure.
从 (two people following each other) — together with the frame above, 两 shows a pair joined together, giving its meaning 'two' or 'both.'
耂 is a variant of 老 (aged, experienced) forming the top of the character.
白 (white, clear) sits below — the ancient combination is debated, but together it came to mark 'the one who' or 'a person who does something,' as in 两者 'the two of them.'

example.hanzi: 两者之间没有明显的区别。
example.pinyin: Liǎngzhě zhī jiān méiyǒu míngxiǎn de qūbié.
example.english: There is no obvious difference between the two of them.
example.fact: Light behaves as both a wave and a particle, a duality confirmed by the double-slit experiment first performed with light by Thomas Young in 1801 and later shown to hold even for individual photons and electrons. Neither description alone is complete — physicists still rely on both models depending on which phenomenon they need to predict.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 计 relates to counting or planning through words and numbers.
十 (shí) gives a hint of the sound — 计 is pronounced jì, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
⺮ (bamboo) — the material of ancient counting rods.
具 (held in two hands) — bamboo counting rods or an abacus held up for use, the tools of calculation that gave 算 its meaning 'to calculate, count.'

example.hanzi: 这台电脑可以快速计算复杂的数据。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái diànnǎo kěyǐ kuàisù jìsuàn fùzá de shùjù.
example.english: This computer can quickly calculate complex data.
example.fact: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from a Greek shipwreck in 1901, is a hand-cranked bronze device built around 150-100 BC that could predict eclipses and track the positions of the sun, moon, and planets — historians consider it the world's oldest known analog computer.

components.note: 八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
寸 here depicts a hand.
良 pictures a goblet — together, a hand holding a ceremonial wine goblet, the image behind 爵's original meaning 'noble rank.'

example.hanzi: 他被国王封为公爵。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi guówáng fēng wéi gōngjué.
example.english: He was made a duke by the king.
example.fact: The title 'duke' derives from the Latin 'dux,' meaning military leader, originally given to Roman provincial commanders. In the United Kingdom today, only a handful of non-royal dukedoms remain, and the rank still sits just below the monarch and above every other hereditary peerage.

meanings: variant of 收穫|收获[shou1 huo4]

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
艹 (grass) — 获 relates to harvesting crops from the field.
又 (a hand) — a hand grasping and gathering, reinforcing 获's meaning 'to obtain, to harvest, to gain.'

example.hanzi: 农民在秋天收获稻子。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín zài qiūtiān shōuhuò dàozi.
example.english: Farmers harvest rice in the autumn.
example.fact: The mechanical combine harvester, invented in the United States in the 1830s, let a single machine cut, thresh, and clean grain in one pass — a task that had previously required dozens of laborers with scythes. Modern combines can harvest an acre of wheat in under six minutes.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — the sickness radical, depicting a person lying on a sickbed — marking the character as related to illness.
隐 (yǐn) gives the sound — an exact match with 瘾's reading.
尹 depicts a hand holding a staff of authority, a leader.
口 (mouth) — a leader giving spoken orders gave 君 its meaning 'ruler, monarch.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 那个瘾君子已经戒毒三年了。
example.pinyin: Nàge yǐnjūnzǐ yǐjīng jièdú sān nián le.
example.english: That addict has been drug-free for three years now.
example.fact: In the 1970s, psychologist Bruce Alexander's 'Rat Park' experiment found that rats given free access to morphine-laced water used it far less when housed in a stimulating, social enclosure than rats isolated in bare cages — suggesting that environment and social connection play a major role in compulsive drug use, not the drug's chemistry alone.

components.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a rider.
可 here is said to depict a mount — a person riding in an unusual way gave 奇 its meaning 'strange, odd, remarkable.'
女 (woman) — 妙 originally described a young woman's delicate charm, extended to mean 'wonderful, clever.'
少 (shǎo) gives a sound distantly related to miào, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 大自然充满了奇妙的现象。
example.pinyin: Dàzìrán chōngmǎn le qímiào de xiànxiàng.
example.english: Nature is full of marvelous phenomena.
example.fact: Bioluminescent plankton called dinoflagellates emit a ghostly blue glow when disturbed by waves or swimmers, a chemical reaction that likely evolved as a defense to startle predators or attract the predator's own predators. Beaches in the Maldives and parts of Australia are famous for these glowing 'sea sparkle' tides.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 消's meaning 'to disappear, dissolve,' like something dissolving in water.
肖 (xiào) gives a sound hint — 消 is pronounced xiāo, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
阝 (a mound/settlement) — represents a city or town.
余 (surplus, remainder) — the leftover waste a city produces, which must be cleared away, giving 除 its meaning 'to remove, eliminate.'

example.hanzi: 疫苗帮助消除了许多传染病。
example.pinyin: Yìmiáo bāngzhù xiāochú le xǔduō chuánrǎnbìng.
example.english: Vaccines have helped eliminate many infectious diseases.
example.fact: Smallpox is the only human disease ever fully eradicated, declared eliminated worldwide by the World Health Organization in 1980 after a global vaccination campaign. The last natural case occurred in Somalia in 1977, and the virus now exists only in two high-security laboratories, in the United States and Russia.

components.note: 宀 (walls/roof) — the boundary of a home to be protected
寸 (a hand) — keeping watch, holding the space within the walls

卫 is a modern simplification of 衛, which pictured feet patrolling around a walled area. The abstracted simplified form keeps that meaning, 'to guard, defend,' without a clear internal split into pieces.

example.hanzi: 士兵在城门口守卫。
example.pinyin: Shìbīng zài chéngmén kǒu shǒuwèi.
example.english: The soldiers guard the city gate.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army, buried around 210 BC to guard the tomb of China's first emperor Qin Shi Huang, consists of over 8,000 life-sized clay soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features. It was discovered by farmers digging a well in 1974 near Xi'an.

components.note: Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'

example.hanzi: 你是不是忘记带伞了?
example.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì wàngjì dài sǎn le?
example.english: Did you forget to bring an umbrella?
example.fact: Transport for London's lost-property office reports collecting tens of thousands of umbrellas in a single year across the city's transit system — more than almost any other item besides phones and keys, according to its annual reports.

meanings: to act on behalf of sb in a responsible position
to act as an agent or proxy

components.note: 亻 (person) — 代 relates to a person's place in time.
弋 (a stake used to mark or catch something) — combined with 亻 (person), 代 came to mean a 'generation' or 'era,' and 'to take the place of' someone.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他委托律师代理这场官司。
example.pinyin: Tā wěituō lǜshī dàilǐ zhè chǎng guānsī.
example.english: He appointed a lawyer to act as his representative in the lawsuit.
example.fact: In computer networking, a proxy server sits between a user and the internet, forwarding requests on the user's behalf — a concept first widely implemented in the early 1990s to cache web pages and speed up slow dial-up connections, long before it became a common tool for privacy and content filtering.

components.note: 宀 (a roof) on top represents an enclosed structure.
牛 (cattle) below is the animal kept inside, giving 牢 its meaning 'pen, stable' and later 'prison.'
户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 房 is pronounced fáng, a close match

example.hanzi: 犯人被关在狭小的牢房里。
example.pinyin: Fànrén bèi guān zài xiáxiǎo de láofáng lǐ.
example.english: The prisoner was locked in a cramped jail cell.
example.fact: Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary in San Francisco Bay, which operated from 1934 to 1963, was considered virtually escape-proof due to the cold, fast currents around the island. In 1962 three inmates famously escaped using papier-mâché head decoys, and their fate remains officially unresolved to this day.

components.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'

example.hanzi: 良好的天气对比赛非常有利。
example.pinyin: Liánghǎo de tiānqì duì bǐsài fēicháng yǒulì.
example.english: Good weather is very advantageous for the competition.
example.fact: Marathon world records are almost always set on flat, cool courses with a slight tailwind, since even a small elevation gain or headwind measurably slows runners. That's why pancake-flat cities like Berlin and Chicago have hosted far more record-breaking marathons than hillier cities like Boston.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 排 relates to arranging things by hand into order
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to 排's reading pái, having drifted apart over time
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'

example.hanzi: 大家都在排队买票。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zài páiduì mǎi piào.
example.english: Everyone is lining up to buy tickets.
example.fact: Queueing theory, the mathematical study of waiting lines, was pioneered by Danish engineer Agner Krarup Erlang in 1909 while analyzing telephone traffic at the Copenhagen Telephone Company. His formulas are still used today to design call centers, hospital triage systems, and amusement park ride lines.

components.note: 女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) gives the sound — 然 is also pronounced rán, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 快点走,要不然我们会迟到。
example.pinyin: Kuài diǎn zǒu, yàobùrán wǒmen huì chídào.
example.english: Hurry up, or else we'll be late.
example.fact: Tokyo's train system is famous for its punctuality, with average delays measured in seconds rather than minutes. In 2017 a train operator publicly apologized after a train departed 20 seconds early, a small illustration of how tightly the country's rail schedules are run compared to systems elsewhere.

components.note: 厂 (a building) — 厨 names a room in a building, the kitchen.
豆 (dòu) gives a sound distantly related to 厨's reading chú, having drifted apart over time.
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'

example.hanzi: 这位厨师做的菜非常美味。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi chúshī zuò de cài fēicháng měiwèi.
example.english: The dishes this chef makes are extremely delicious.
example.fact: The tall, pleated white hat traditionally worn by chefs, the toque, is said to date to the 16th century, when cooks fleeing religious persecution in the Byzantine Empire hid in Orthodox monasteries and adopted the tall hats worn by monks. The hat's height later became a way to signal rank, with head chefs wearing taller toques than junior cooks.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 捐 describes giving something with one's hands, donating.
肙 (juān) gives the sound — an exact match with 捐.
贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赠 relates to giving something of value.
曾 (zēng) gives the sound — an exact match with 赠, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他捐赠了大量资金给医院。
example.pinyin: Tā juānzèng le dàliàng zījīn gěi yīyuàn.
example.english: He donated a large sum of money to the hospital.
example.fact: The Giving Pledge, launched by Warren Buffett and Bill and Melinda Gates in 2010, asks billionaires to commit at least half their wealth to charity, either during their lifetime or in their will. As of the mid-2020s, more than 200 individuals and families across over 20 countries had signed on.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 例 relates to an example or precedent set by a particular case
列 (liè) gives a sound close to 例's reading lì, sharing the same initial consonant and tone
女 (woman) — depicts a wife in the traditional image behind this character.
口 (mouth/words) — the wife following her husband's spoken words gave 如 its meaning of 'as, like, if.'

example.hanzi: 许多水果,例如苹果和香蕉,都富含维生素。
example.pinyin: Xǔduō shuǐguǒ, lìrú píngguǒ hé xiāngjiāo, dōu fùhán wéishēngsù.
example.english: Many fruits, for example apples and bananas, are rich in vitamins.
example.fact: Scurvy, caused by vitamin C deficiency, plagued sailors on long ocean voyages for centuries until Scottish physician James Lind ran one of the first controlled clinical trials in 1747, proving that citrus fruits like limes and lemons could cure and prevent it — decades before vitamins were even understood as a concept.

components.note: 夂 depicts a foot trailing behind, the image of a person trudging slowly forward.
⺀ depicts two small drops standing for ice — combined with the trudging foot 夂, it pictures walking through the cold, giving 冬 its meaning 'winter.'
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 北方的冬天非常寒冷。
example.pinyin: Běifāng de dōngtiān fēicháng hánlěng.
example.english: Winters in the north are extremely cold.
example.fact: The coldest inhabited place on Earth is the Siberian town of Oymyakon, Russia, where temperatures have dropped as low as -67.7°C (-89.9°F). Despite this, around 500 people still live there year-round, keeping their cars running constantly since engines can crack if turned off in the deep winter.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 婚礼上的场面十分壮观。
example.pinyin: Hūnlǐ shàng de chǎngmiàn shífēn zhuàngguān.
example.english: The scene at the wedding was truly spectacular.
example.fact: The opening ceremony of the 2008 Beijing Olympics involved over 15,000 performers and featured a giant unrolling scroll made of LED screens. Directed by filmmaker Zhang Yimou, it remains one of the most expensive opening ceremonies in Olympic history, reportedly costing over $100 million.

meanings: to be in the prime of life

components.note: 当 is a simplified form of 當, which combined 田 (a field) with a phonetic element. Comparing equal plots of farmland gave rise to the meaning 'to correspond to, to be equal to,' later broadening to 'to serve as' and, in 当年, 'in those years.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 当年他还只是一个学生。
example.pinyin: Dāngnián tā hái zhǐshì yí gè xuéshēng.
example.english: Back then, he was still just a student.
example.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 lasted only 12 seconds and covered 120 feet, shorter than the wingspan of a modern Boeing 747. Just 66 years later, in 1969, humans landed on the Moon — a pace of change historians often cite as one of the fastest in human history.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 纯 originally described unmixed, undyed silk thread, extending to 'pure, unmixed.'
屯 (tún) gives a sound distantly related to chún, having drifted apart over time.
Rice/grain — relates to something refined, like husked grain.
Gives the sound zú, related to cuì but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这是纯粹的巧合。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì chúncuì de qiǎohé.
example.english: This is pure coincidence.
example.fact: Gold with a purity of 24 karats is considered 'pure gold,' containing no other metals, but because pure gold is very soft, jewelry is usually made with 18K or 14K gold alloyed with metals like copper or silver to increase durability and change its color slightly.

components.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
乂 (a hand holding a writing tool) — the act of recording events, giving 史 its meaning 'history, chronicle.'
人 (a person) — depicts someone carrying something.
厶 represents a tool or bundle being carried — a person holding an implement to use, giving 以 its meaning 'to use, by means of, in order to.'
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 这是有史以来最热的一年。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yǒushǐyǐlái zuì rè de yì nián.
example.english: This is the hottest year since records began.
example.fact: According to NASA and NOAA climate records extending back to 1880, the ten warmest years ever recorded have all occurred since 2010, with global average temperatures now roughly 1.1-1.2°C above the pre-industrial baseline used by climate scientists.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 约 originally meant 'to bind, tie up,' extending to 'to agree, arrange' and 'approximately.'
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 我们约定明天下午见面。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yuēdìng míngtiān xiàwǔ jiànmiàn.
example.english: We agreed to meet tomorrow afternoon.
example.fact: The Geneva Conventions, first adopted in 1864 and expanded after both World Wars, establish international standards for humanitarian treatment during war. Nearly every country in the world, 196 in total, is now a party to them, making them among the most universally ratified treaties in history.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/wall) — 防 relates to defensive walls and prevention
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 防 is also pronounced fáng, a close match
止 depicts a footprint, with toes at the top and the leg below — a simple picture of a foot, later extended to mean 'to stop.'

example.hanzi: 洗手可以防止细菌传播。
example.pinyin: Xǐshǒu kěyǐ fángzhǐ xìjūn chuánbò.
example.english: Washing your hands can prevent the spread of germs.
example.fact: In 1847, Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis found that hospital deaths from childbed fever dropped dramatically when doctors washed their hands with chlorinated lime before examining patients. His colleagues largely rejected the idea since germ theory wasn't yet accepted, and he died in an asylum before handwashing became standard medical practice decades later.

components.note: 无 is a simplification of 無, which originally pictured a dancer waving tasseled sleeves in a ritual dance meant to invoke rain. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to mean 'without, not have,' and its original dance sense was replaced by 舞.

关 is a simplification of 關, which pictured a gate (門) barred shut by a threaded bolt. The simplified form kept only an abstracted version of the bolt, retaining the meaning 'to close, to bar' and, by extension, 'to be concerned with.'
糸 (silk/thread) — 紧 relates to something pulled taut, as thread is pulled tight when spun, giving its meaning 'tight, tense'
女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'

example.hanzi: 这些细节其实无关紧要。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē xìjié qíshí wúguānjǐnyào.
example.english: These details are actually insignificant.
example.fact: The 'butterfly effect,' a term coined by meteorologist Edward Lorenz in the 1960s, describes how a seemingly insignificant change — like rounding a number in a weather simulation from six decimal places to three — can lead to wildly different long-term outcomes, a discovery that helped found the field of chaos theory.

meanings: to have an instant attraction to sb
(of electricity, after an outage) to come back

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'

example.hanzi: 手机显示有一个来电。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī xiǎnshì yǒu yí gè láidiàn.
example.english: The phone shows there is an incoming call.
example.fact: The first mobile phone call was made in April 1973 by Motorola engineer Martin Cooper, who called a rival researcher at Bell Labs while standing on a New York City street with a prototype handset that weighed over a kilogram and offered just 30 minutes of talk time per charge.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
广 (a shelter or lean-to) forms the top of this character.

应 is a simplification of 應, which paired 心 (heart, one's inner response) with a phonetic element derived from 雁 (wild goose). The simplified form keeps only the abstracted shelter-like shape, retaining the meaning 'to respond, should.'

example.hanzi: 他常说做坏事迟早会有报应。
example.pinyin: Tā cháng shuō zuò huàishì chízǎo huì yǒu bàoyìng.
example.english: He often says that doing bad things will eventually have consequences.
example.fact: The concept of karma originates in ancient Indian religious traditions, appearing in Hindu texts like the Upanishads composed as early as 800 BCE, where it described a cosmic law of cause and effect governing actions across multiple lifetimes — long before the word entered everyday English as shorthand for 'what goes around comes around.'

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 我们计划去海边度假。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà qù hǎibiān dùjià.
example.english: We're planning to go on vacation at the seaside.
example.fact: The Dead Sea's shoreline, about 430 meters below sea level, is the lowest point on Earth's land surface accessible on foot. Its extremely high salt concentration, nearly ten times saltier than the ocean, lets swimmers float on the surface almost without effort.

components.note: 艹 (grass) forms the top of the character.
木 (tree), sheltered beneath a covering, together depict plants flourishing, giving 荣 its meaning 'glory, prosperity.'
Light — represents brightness.
A bird with long, shining feathers, like a peacock's tail.

example.hanzi: 赢得冠军是全队的荣耀。
example.pinyin: Yíngdé guànjūn shì quán duì de róngyào.
example.english: Winning the championship is an honor for the whole team.
example.fact: Ancient Olympic champions in Greece received only an olive wreath cut from a sacred tree near the Temple of Zeus at Olympia, yet victors often received lifelong honors back home, including free meals, tax exemptions, and statues erected in their likeness — glory mattered more than material prizes.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 脑 refers to the brain, a part of the body
氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 那个画面一直浮现在我的脑海中。
example.pinyin: Nàge huàmiàn yìzhí fúxiàn zài wǒ de nǎohǎi zhōng.
example.english: That image keeps surfacing in my mind.
example.fact: The human brain generates roughly 20 watts of power, enough to dimly light a small LED bulb, yet it consumes about 20% of the body's total energy despite making up only around 2% of body weight — a reminder of how metabolically expensive thought and memory actually are.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 控 relates to controlling or restraining something by hand
空 (kōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 控's reading kòng
口 (mouth) — the act of speaking.
牛 (ox) — traditionally read as speaking with the forceful weight of an ox, giving 告 its meaning 'to tell, announce, inform.'

example.hanzi: 她向法院控告这家公司欺诈。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng fǎyuàn kònggào zhè jiā gōngsī qīzhà.
example.english: She accused the company of fraud in court.
example.fact: The Salem witch trials of 1692-93 in colonial Massachusetts saw over 200 people accused of witchcraft based largely on testimony now understood as mass hysteria; 19 were executed before the governor intervened. Massachusetts didn't formally apologize and clear the names of all the accused until 2022, 330 years later.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 镇 originally referred to a heavy metal weight used to press something down, later extending to 'garrison town.'
真 (zhēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 镇's reading zhèn, differing only in tone.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 这个小镇子只有几百口人。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo zhènzi zhǐyǒu jǐ bǎi kǒu rén.
example.english: This small town only has a few hundred people.
example.fact: Whittier, Alaska, is a small town where nearly the entire population of around 200 people lives inside a single 14-story former U.S. Army building called Begich Towers, sharing one building for homes, the police station, a school, and a grocery store — largely due to the extreme winter isolation of the area.

components.note: 车 (a vehicle) — 轿 refers to a carried vehicle, a sedan chair.
乔 depicts something tall or lofty, describing the raised seat of a sedan chair.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 他新买了一辆红色轿车。
example.pinyin: Tā xīn mǎi le yí liàng hóngsè jiàochē.
example.english: He just bought a new red sedan.
example.fact: The Ford Model T, produced from 1908 to 1927, was the first car mass-produced on a moving assembly line, cutting the time to build one chassis from over 12 hours to about 93 minutes. The resulting drop in price made car ownership possible for millions of ordinary American families for the first time.

components.note: 走 (to walk/run) — 超 relates to overtaking or surpassing someone while moving
召 (zhào) gives a sound distantly related to 超's reading chāo, having drifted apart over time
走 (run/walk) — relates to 越's meaning 'to exceed, cross over,' running past a boundary.
戉 (yuè) gives the sound — 越 is also pronounced yuè, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他的成绩超越了所有人的预期。
example.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì chāoyuè le suǒyǒu rén de yùqí.
example.english: His results surpassed everyone's expectations.
example.fact: Usain Bolt's 2009 world record of 9.58 seconds in the 100-meter sprint remains unbroken as of the mid-2020s. Biomechanical analysis showed he reached a peak speed of about 27.8 mph (44.7 km/h) partway through the race, among the fastest a human has ever been recorded running.

components.note: 日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.

example.hanzi: 他明明知道答案,却不说。
example.pinyin: Tā míngmíng zhīdào dá'àn, què bù shuō.
example.english: He obviously knew the answer, but didn't say it.
example.fact: The Dunning-Kruger effect, described by psychologists Justin Kruger and David Dunning in 1999, found that people with low competence in a skill often overestimate their ability more than experts do — meaning the people most obviously wrong about something are frequently the least aware of it.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — caution here is expressed carefully in what one says.
堇 (jǐn) gives the sound — an exact match for 谨.
Heart — being careful involves a thoughtful mind.
Gives a sound distantly related to shèn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 投资的时候一定要谨慎。
example.pinyin: Tóuzī de shíhòu yídìng yào jǐnshèn.
example.english: You must be cautious when investing.
example.fact: Nuclear reactor operators follow a principle called 'defense in depth,' which stacks multiple independent, redundant safety systems so that no single failure can cause a meltdown. The approach was reinforced further after the 1979 Three Mile Island accident and again after Fukushima in 2011, each time adding new layers of caution to reactor design worldwide.

components.note: 亼 depicts a lid coming down to cover an opening.
口 (an opening/container) — a lid fitting snugly over a container's mouth gave 合 its meaning 'to close, to combine, to fit together.'
纟 (thread) — 约 originally meant 'to bind, tie up,' extending to 'to agree, arrange' and 'approximately.'

example.hanzi: 双方已经签订了合约。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng yǐjīng qiāndìng le héyuē.
example.english: Both parties have already signed the contract.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a basalt stele around 1754 BC in ancient Babylon, is one of the oldest surviving written legal codes. It included detailed rules governing contracts for trade, loans, and labor, showing that formal, enforceable agreements between parties are one of civilization's oldest legal inventions.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 植 relates to planting trees and other plants.
直 (zhí) gives the sound — an exact match with 植's reading zhí.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 阳光对植物的生长非常重要。
example.pinyin: Yángguāng duì zhíwù de shēngzhǎng fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.english: Sunlight is very important for plant growth.
example.fact: The Pando aspen colony in Utah is a single organism made up of over 40,000 genetically identical tree trunks connected by one shared root system, covering about 106 acres and estimated to be thousands of years old — one of the largest and oldest living organisms on Earth.

components.note: 宀 (a roof) — represents a building or residence.
The lower portion is traditionally read as a stack of mounds or dwellings, depicting a cluster of government buildings — together giving 官 its meaning 'official, officer, government post.'
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 政府官员出席了这次会议。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ guānyuán chūxí le zhè cì huìyì.
example.english: Government officials attended this meeting.
example.fact: Imperial China's civil service examination system, which selected government officials based on merit through rigorous written tests on classical texts, ran in some form for roughly 1,300 years, from the Sui dynasty until it was abolished in 1905 — one of history's longest-running standardized meritocratic institutions.

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 原 relates to a source high up, such as a spring emerging from rock.
泉 (quán) gives a hint of the sound — 原 is pronounced yuán, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
女 (woman) — 始's meaning 'beginning' has been linked to the idea of the origin of life.
台 (tái) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shǐ.

example.hanzi: 考古学家发现了原始人类使用的工具。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā fāxiàn le yuánshǐ rénlèi shǐyòng de gōngjù.
example.english: Archaeologists discovered tools used by primitive humans.
example.fact: The Lomekwi 3 site in Kenya contains stone tools dated to about 3.3 million years ago, predating the genus Homo entirely — meaning some of the earliest known toolmakers may have been australopithecines, not humans, pushing back the origin of technology far earlier than scientists once assumed.

meanings: world of a particular locale and era

components.note: 日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form
穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 爱因斯坦的理论改变了我们对时空的理解。
example.pinyin: Àiyīnsītǎn de lǐlùn gǎibiàn le wǒmen duì shíkōng de lǐjiě.
example.english: Einstein's theory changed our understanding of space-time.
example.fact: Einstein's general theory of relativity, published in 1915, describes gravity not as a force but as the curvature of four-dimensional space-time caused by mass. That prediction was confirmed in 2015 when the LIGO observatory directly detected gravitational waves rippling through space-time from two colliding black holes over a billion light-years away.

components.note: 岂 pictures a ceremonial drum raised on a stand, played to celebrate a military victory.
几 (a small stand or table) supports the drum, together giving 凯 its meaning 'triumphant, victorious' — used here purely for its sound in the transliterated name 凯瑟琳.
玨 (two connected jade pieces, standing in for strings) shows 瑟 relates to a stringed instrument.
必 (bì) gives a sound distantly related to sè, having drifted apart over time.
王 (jade, written as 王 in components) — 琳 describes a fine jade or gem.
林 (lín) gives the sound — an exact match with 琳.

example.hanzi: 凯瑟琳是这所学校最优秀的学生。
example.pinyin: Kǎisèlín shì zhè suǒ xuéxiào zuì yōuxiù de xuéshēng.
example.english: Catherine is the best student at this school.
example.fact: Catherine the Great ruled the Russian Empire from 1762 to 1796, the longest reign of any female ruler in Russian history, and oversaw a massive territorial expansion that added over 200,000 square miles to the empire, including much of modern-day Ukraine and Crimea.

components.note: 礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.
纟 (silk/thread) — 经 originally referred to the vertical warp threads in weaving.
工 (gōng) gives a related sound cue for 经 (jīng), reflecting an older, closer pronunciation link between the two.
疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 长期糖尿病可能引发神经病。
example.pinyin: Chángqī tángniàobìng kěnéng yǐnfā shénjīngbìng.
example.english: Long-term diabetes can lead to neuropathy.
example.fact: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy, nerve damage caused by prolonged high blood sugar, affects roughly half of all people with diabetes at some point and is one of the leading causes of numbness and pain in the feet and hands worldwide, according to the World Health Organization.

meanings: plastics (general term for synthetic polymer materials)

components.note: 土 (earth) — sculpting was traditionally done with clay, a form of earth.
朔 (shuò) gives a sound moderately close to sù, sharing the initial consonant family.
米 (rice) — the grain being measured.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring out rice gave 料 its meaning 'material, to estimate, to reckon.'

example.hanzi: 海洋里漂浮着大量塑料垃圾。
example.pinyin: Hǎiyáng lǐ piāofú zhe dàliàng sùliào lājī.
example.english: Large amounts of plastic waste float in the ocean.
example.fact: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch, a floating accumulation of plastic debris in the North Pacific Ocean, is estimated to cover an area roughly three times the size of France — though it is not a solid island but a diffuse zone where plastic concentration is far higher than in the surrounding water.
